unsupported_wording: 'screened plant' is in the development description, not a screening condition. The parapet condition (Cond. 9) bars 'lift motor enclosures, air handling equipment, storage tanks, ducts or other external plant' above parapet level unless further permission is granted, so this is supported. The flue-stack finishes are not set by the condition. Cond. 6(a) requires the finishes, including to the flue stacks, to be agreed in writing with the planning authority, with samples. No colour or material is fixed.
note: Dublin 15 comes from the An Bord Pleanála case page, not the order itself.

values.quote: Generation and Energy Storage Projects ... *55 Weeks ... 14 Weeks ... 30 Weeks ... 39 Weeks

unsupported_wording: The text extraction of the graphic is jumbled, so it is uncertain which week figures go with generation/storage and which go with load/reliability (51/34/41/15/2). Check the PDF visually. The guide does not say 'only where transmission is needed'. It says the process 'is followed when the AESO determines that a System Access Service Request (SASR) will require the addition or alteration of facilities on Alberta's transmission system', so the claim's phrase is a paraphrase. The guide labels these 'target timelines', not 'indicative weeks'.
note: AESO targets are not achieved durations. The April 2026 performance update reports actual times well above the targets.

url: https://free.bcpublications.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/200_2003 (bclaws.gov.bc.ca link not fetchable from this session; same King's Printer consolidation)

values.quote: the system does not provide water for human consumption or food preparation purposes ... is not connected to a water supply system that provides water for human consumption ... identified by markings that are permanent, distinct and easily recognized
may issue a construction permit to a person after receiving an application (s. 6(2)); may issue an operating permit to a water supplier after receiving an application (s. 7(1))

unsupported_wording: The regulation sets out how permits are issued and when they are exempt. The duty itself ('a water supplier needs construction and operating permits') is in the Drinking Water Protection Act (ss. 7–8), not this regulation. The s. 3.1 exemption applies only to s. 6 of the Act. The blank structure 's. ___ ___(b), ___–___' is ambiguous, so my mapping to 3.1(b) and 6–7 is an inference.
note: I read the free.bcpublications.ca copy because the bclaws.gov.bc.ca URL was blocked by fetch provenance rules. It is the same official consolidation.
